questions.stem_text: Which of the following does authentication aim to accomplish?

options.A: Restrict what operations/data the user can access
options.B: Determine if the user is an attacker
options.C: Flag the user if he/she misbehaves

questions.answer_explanation: Authentication aims to determine who the user is by verifying their identity through various methods, ensuring that access to systems and data is granted only to authorized individuals.

questions.stem_text: 1. _________ framework made cracking of vulnerabilities easy like point and click.
questions.answer_explanation: Metasploit is a widely used penetration testing framework that simplifies the exploitation of vulnerabilities through its user-friendly interface, enabling users to perform attacks with minimal technical expertise.

questions.stem_text: A Base Transceiver Station (BTS) provides wireless communication coverage for mobile operators, similar to an Access Point in Wi-Fi networks.
questions.answer_explanation: A Base Transceiver Station (BTS) facilitates wireless communication for mobile operators by connecting mobile devices to the network, analogous to how an Access Point connects Wi-Fi devices to a local area network.

questions.stem_text: A buffer overflow occurs when a program rejects requests after detecting that a buffer has filled up.
questions.answer_explanation: A buffer overflow occurs when a program writes more data to a buffer than it can hold, leading to unintended memory corruption, rather than rejecting requests when a buffer is full.

questions.stem_text: The one-time pad is considered a perfectly secure encryption scheme when used correctly and with truly random keys.
questions.answer_explanation: The one-time pad is considered perfectly secure because it uses a key that is as long as the message, is truly random, and is used only once, ensuring that the ciphertext does not reveal any information about the plaintext without knowledge of the key.

questions.stem_text: A fixed-length MAC tag of 5 bits can provide sufficient security against all types of cryptographic attacks.
questions.answer_explanation: A fixed-length MAC tag of 5 bits is too short to provide sufficient security, as it only allows for 32 possible unique tags, making it vulnerable to brute-force and collision attacks.

questions.stem_text: The sub key length at each round of DES is 48 bits, derived from a 56-bit key through the key schedule algorithm.
questions.answer_explanation: In the Data Encryption Standard (DES), the key schedule algorithm processes a 56-bit key to produce a series of 48-bit subkeys used in each of the 16 rounds of encryption.
